subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.

spec.name: Calder Hanging Mobile
spec.description: A Calder-style hanging mobile: black wire arms nested five tiers deep, balanced on solder knots, carrying flat painted sheet-metal discs and leaves in red, blue, yellow, black and white.
spec.layout: The mobile hangs from a ceiling canopy at the very top (y=2.4); its lowest shape bottoms out near y=0.25 and nothing rests on the floor. The main arm A (a thin black wire, about 1.7 m long) sits at y=1.95 and hangs off a single wire from the ceiling hook at x=0. It has a long arm to +X (the model's left) and a short one to -X, yawed about 12 degrees in plan, so the whole mobile reads as a 3D drifting composition and not a flat drawing. From the +X end of A, a wire drops to the pivot of arm B (y=1.4, yawed about -30 degrees). Arm B carries a big red disc on its +X end (the anchor shape, radius 0.28, hanging furthest right) and, on its -X end, a wire dropping to arm D (y=1.0, yawed about 20 degrees). Arm D carries a black leaf (tall, narrow, 0.48 high) on its -X end and a smaller yellow disc on its +X end. From the -X end of A, a wire drops to the pivot of long arm C (y=1.2, yawed about 25 degrees, reaching to x=-1.5). Arm C carries a big blue leaf or kidney shape on its far -X end and, on its short +X end, a wire dropping to arm E (y=0.85, yawed about -20 degrees). Arm E carries a small white disc with a black ring on its -X end and a black teardrop (the lowest element, bottom at y=0.25) on its +X end. Lengths of the wire drops are varied: some short, some long. Style: Alexander Calder. Every arm and drop is a thin dark wire (radius 0.005 to 0.008) with small bent hook loops (tiny torus rings) at the ends and brass solder knots (tiny spheres) at each pivot and joint. Every shape is a flat, thin cut-metal plate (extrude thickness about 0.012 to 0.018, with a small bevel). Each plate has a slightly bigger, darker 'deep' plate behind it, offset 0.004, so the edge reads as a painted rim. The shapes are matte flat primary colours. Small details are separate parts seated on the plates: a white dot row on the red disc, a black quarter-circle cut-out on the yellow disc, a thin white stripe on the blue leaf, a white centre dot on the black leaf, a black ring on the white disc, and a red bead on arm E. Shapes hang in different orientations: yaw them 20 to 70 degrees around the vertical so no two face the same way, and tilt each a few degrees. Plates have bold, simple outlines: a circle, a leaf, a kidney, a teardrop. Use only palette colours.

parts.builds: The top of the mobile. A thin round ceiling canopy (a lathe or flat cylinder in ceiling with a ceilingEdge rim ring and a small screw head), a wire hook eye (torus in wire) at hookEye, and the suspension wire down to the armA pivot with a solder knot. Main arm A: a long thin wire rod from armAEndL to armAEndR through armAPivot, with a hook loop ring at each end, a solder collar at the pivot, and a small black bead counterweight near the short end. Two hanging wires with hook loops at both ends: one from armAEndR down to pivotB, one from armAEndL down to pivotC. Wire is in wire, with a few thin wireHighlight rods alongside for gleam. Brass solder blobs at every knot. No shapes hang here.
parts.attaches: The wire to pivotB ends at the loop on arm B (branchB); the wire to pivotC ends at the loop on arm C (branchC). The arm A joint is armA; the canopy and hook ride mobile.

parts.builds: Arm B: a wire rod from armBEnd1 to armBEnd2 through pivotB, with a loop at pivotB to take the wire from crown, hook loops at both ends and a solder knot. At armBEnd2 a drop wire with hook loops goes down to redDiscTop, carrying the big red disc: a circle of radius 0.28 and thickness 0.015, yawed about 50 degrees, with a redDeep plate behind it (radius 0.285, offset 0.004), a ring of small white dots (about 10) near the rim, and a black quarter-circle cut-out wedge (flat sheet in black) near the centre. At armBEnd1 a drop wire with hook loops goes down to the pivotD loop, where arm D (branchD) takes over. The red disc rides redDisc and the arm rides armB.
parts.attaches: pivotB is where crown's wire ends. The wire to pivotD ends at the loop at the top of arm D. The disc is hooked at redDiscTop.

parts.builds: Arm D: a short wire rod from armDEnd1 to armDEnd2 through pivotD, with a loop at the pivot to take the wire from branchB, hook loops and solder knots. At armDEnd1 a drop wire down to leafBlackTop holds a black leaf plate (tall pointed ellipse, 0.48 high, 0.2 wide, thickness 0.014, yawed 70 degrees) with a blackDeep plate behind it, a white centre dot, and a thin white midrib line. At armDEnd2 a drop wire down to discYellowTop holds a yellow disc (radius 0.15, yawed -30 degrees, tilted slightly) with a yellowDeep plate behind it, a black quarter-circle cut-out wedge and a tiny black dot. Leaf rides leafBlack, disc rides discYellow, arm rides armD.
parts.attaches: pivotD is where branchB's wire ends. Shapes hook at leafBlackTop and discYellowTop.

parts.builds: Arm C: the longest lower arm, a wire rod from armCEnd1 (far -X) to armCEnd2 through pivotC, with a loop at the pivot to take the wire from crown, hook loops and solder knots at the pivot and both ends. At armCEnd1 a long drop wire down to leafBlueTop holds the big blue leaf or kidney plate (about 0.55 high, 0.34 wide, thickness 0.016, yawed 20 degrees) with a blueDeep plate behind it, a thin white stripe sweeping along the plate, and a few small white dots. At armCEnd2 a drop wire with hook loops goes down to the pivotE loop, where arm E (branchE) takes over. The leaf rides leafBlue, the arm rides armC.
parts.attaches: pivotC is where crown's wire ends. The wire to pivotE ends at the loop at the top of arm E. The leaf hooks at leafBlueTop.

parts.builds: Arm E: a short wire rod from armEEnd1 to armEEnd2 through pivotE, with a loop at the pivot to take the wire from branchC, hook loops and solder knots, and a small red bead on the arm near pivotE. At armEEnd1 a drop wire down to discWhiteTop holds a small white disc (radius 0.12, thickness 0.012, yawed 40 degrees) with a whiteDeep plate behind it and a thin black ring seated on its face. At armEEnd2 a long drop wire down to dropBlackTop holds a black teardrop plate (0.3 high, 0.17 wide at the round end, pointed at the top, thickness 0.014, yawed -60 degrees) with a blackDeep plate behind it and a small white dot; this is the lowest element, bottom at y=0.25. The disc rides discWhite, the drop rides dropBlack, the arm rides armE.
parts.attaches: pivotE is where branchC's wire ends. Shapes hook at discWhiteTop and dropBlackTop.

calls.reasoning:
I'm thinking through how to design the Calder-style hanging mobile, working out how the hierarchy of arms and wires should balance and what it means for it to hang at a fixed height above the ground.

I'm settling on a hook and canopy plate at the ceiling with a main horizontal arm around y=1.95, and I'm planning out the branching tiers below it, balancing pivot points so the spread of shapes along x and z feels natural like a real mobile.

I'm organizing the design into clusters: a "crown" piece with the ceiling attachment, hook, main arm, counterweight, and wires dropping to two sub-arms, then a "rightCluster" tier holding a big red disc and black leaf shape hanging further out.

The "leftCluster" tier gets a blue leaf and yellow circle with its own sub-arm of smaller pieces, and I'm working out how to hang a third tier off tier B's other end without crowding the center, assigning pivot points and wire connections between the big disc and a secondary tier D.

I should also decide whether to add joints for a swinging animation, structuring a hierarchy where a root mobile joint parents each arm pivot, with hinge rotation around the vertical axis so arms rotate naturally.

Now I'm mapping out exact coordinates for each tier: the canopy and hook sit near the top around y=2.4, with wire dropping to arm A's pivot at y=1.95, then arm A spanning from roughly x=-0.75 to x=1.0, with slight rotations so the arms don't all align flatly in plan view for a more natural 3D look.

Working through the geometry, I settle on pivot B at [0.95,1.4,0.2], with arm endpoints B_1 [0.55,1.4,0.44] and B_2 [1.3,1.4,-0.01], verifying the slope checks out so the points stay collinear.

From B_2 I'm hanging a wire down to a red disc near [1.3,0.8,-0.01], though I realize the lowest point should sit closer to 0.25 so another branch will need to extend further down. From B_1 I'm dropping a wire to pivot D [0.55,1.0,0.44], branching into a black leaf at D_1 [0.25,1.0,0.34] and a small yellow disc at D_2 [0.85,1.0,0.55].

Checking for overlap, the D shapes occupy x 0.25-0.85, z 0.3-0.6, while the red disc sits further out at x 1.02-1.58, z -0.01, so they're clear of each other. From A_L [-0.7,1.95,-0.15] I'm adding a wire down to pivot C [-0.7,1.2,-0.15] with a long arm yawed 40°, ending at C_1 [-1.15,1.2,0.15] — I need to keep the overall mobile width roughly centered around x=0, spanning about -1.4 to 1.6, which feels appropriately wide for a Calder-style composition.

I'll set the total width to 3.0 with extremes at ±1.5, placing the red disc at x=1.3 (radius 0.28, reaching 1.58) and pushing the left extreme to -1.55. Pivot C at [-0.7,1.2,-0.15] spans to C_1 [-1.5,1.2,0.25] and C_2 [-0.3,1.2,-0.35], maintaining the correct balance ratio between the two arm directions. From C_1 I'm hanging a wire down to a large blue leaf shape at [-1.5,0.55,0.25], and from C_2 a wire down to another pivot E [-0.3,0.85,-0.35], which yaws -20° and ends at E_1 [-0.65,0.85,-0.22] holding a small yellow circle near y=0.

Now I'm placing E_2 at [0.1,0.85,-0.48] hanging a black spiral/teardrop shape with its lowest point around 0.25, giving the whole mobile a height span from about 0.25 to 2.4 and a depth range of roughly -0.7 to 0.7, so overall size comes out to [3.1, 2.4, 1.5]. I'm organizing this into parts: the "crown" piece (ceiling canopy, hook, wire, arm A, loops, counterweight, connecting wires, and small decorative beads) budgeted around 120 units and spanning y 1.85–2.4, followed by a "redBranch" piece covering the Tier B arm and the red disc with its decorative white ring.

Now I'm restructuring into five balanced parts instead: crown, branchB (arm B plus red disc plus wire down to D), branchD (arm D plus black leaf, yellow disc, and related shapes), branchC (arm C plus blue leaf plus wire to E), and branchE (arm E plus its two shapes). I'm assigning budgets of roughly 100 for crown and 170 each for the four branches, totaling about 780, and planning for each shape to have layered detail—flat colored base plus a slightly larger darker rim extrusion plus small accent marks—to keep the richness even across parts.

Setting up the Calder-style palette now: muted wire grays, deep and bright reds, blues, yellows, plus black, white, and a soft ceiling tone, with shapes designed to hang from small wire hooks and eyelet loops for authenticity.

I'm now mapping out the 3D coordinates for the mobile's mounting points and pivot arms, positioning the ceiling plate, hook eye, and the branching wire arms where each hanging shape will attach.

Working out the leaf and disc positions for D_1 and D_2: black leaf centered around y 0.62 with the yellow disc above it at y 0.7, making sure the lowest teardrop point still bottoms out near 0.25.

Now working through the C branch: pivot and arm points for the blue leaf shape, giving it a yaw orientation and wire length from the pivot down to the leaf top. I'm sketching out the E pivot position too, continuing to wire up the remaining mounts.

Rethinking E_1 as a white disc with a ring instead of yellow, and E_2 as a hanging black teardrop; considering a small bead accent too. I'm also sketching the joint hierarchy—mobile root, armA, armB, armC—and their pivot positions.

I'm assigning each hanging shape to its own joint for sway (redDisc, leafBlack, discYellow, leafBlue, discWhite, dropBlack), keeping camelCase naming and letting shapes hang rigidly off their parent arm joints. I'm also working out which part owns the connecting wire between armA and pivot B, since the crown piece spans that gap.

For styling, I'm giving wires a thin radius with slightly thicker arm sweeps and solder-blob joints, small torus loops for hangers, and thin extruded shapes with a darker rim layer for depth -- plus Calder-style surface details like a red disc with a ring of small dots and a quarter-cutout for visual interest.

Now I'm computing bounding boxes for each component of the mobile since it hangs off the ground with no floor contact: the crown piece spans roughly x -0.8 to 1.05 down to y 1.2 where wires connect to pivots, and branch B's box covers its arm, red disc, and connecting wire down toward pivot D's level.

I'm working through branches C and D's dimensions next, noting their blue leaf and wire extensions, then checking branch E's box for overlap with C since their wire connections share space -- adjusting C's x-range slightly to -1.7 to -0.25 and its y-max to 0.8 to keep the overlap limited to just the pivot wire.

Settling on an overall size of [3.2, 2.4, 1.3] with x spanning -1.6 to 1.6, accepting the hanging offset at the lowest point. Now I'm composing the final layout JSON with style notes: thin black wire, flat sheet-metal shapes in matte primary colors, slightly beveled edges, and a two-tone darker backing layer for depth.
